title: serving-runtime-daily-scratchpad-2026-03-06
content:
2026-03-06 - daily scratchpad (personal notes)
Owner: Ethan Cole

Top-of-day goals:
- finish triage and propose mitigation for P0 kernel OOM on long sequences
- validate batching throughput regressions (after Triton upgrade)
- quick follow-up on KV-cache eviction edge case (seen in canary)

1) P0: kernel OOM regression (reported @ 03:20 UTC)
- Symptoms: models with sequence length > 4096 hitting OOM on g5x16 when doing multi-chunk attention. Not reproducible on smaller seqs.
- First suspect: cuBLAS/cuDNN/Triton kernel change (recent infra bump to triton 2.17).
- Repro steps: run reproducer script on g5x16: `./tools/repro_long_seq.sh --model llama-13b --seq 8192 --batch 1` -> OOM at forward pass (ATTN kernel).
- Quick triage notes:
  - try `export TRITON_DISABLE_CONV_FWD=1` (no effect)
  - pin triton to 2.15 in local env -> repro disappears (good signal)
  - check driver/kernel mismatch: nvidia-driver 535.x in prod, same locally.
- Action items:
  - rollback triton on a single canary pool and monitor (assigned to Maya)
  - bisect triton subversion to find breaking change (assign to me)
  - short-term mitigation: add sequence-length cap in routing policy to avoid long sequences hitting dedicated pools until fixed. Patch PR: `serving/runtime: add seq_length_cap config` (WIP).

2) Perf regression: 20% drop in tokens/sec on dedicated (reported yesterday)
- Observed across Llama-7b and Llama-13b. Throughput drop appears correlated with changes to batching heuristics (auto-batching heuristics tuned in #411).
- Metrics summary (prod, avg over 1h before/after):
  - tokens/s before: 820 -> after: 650 (7b, batch target 8)
  - p50 latency increased from 28ms to 34ms
- Hypothesis: new batching heuristic prefers slightly larger batches but increases scheduling latency for small quick requests. Also KV-cache reuse pattern might change batch formation.
- Experiments to run:
  - rollback batching heuristic one flag at a time (flag: `enable_lookahead_batching`)
  - run synthetic workload that mixes short/long prefixes to measure scheduler behavior: `python tools/batch_sim.py --mix 70:30 --qps 120`
  - capture flamegraphs for scheduler and worker threads (perf + `py-spy` for runtime shim)
- Next steps: collect flamegraphs and perf traces (me). If rollback proves low-risk, roll out toggle to 10% and monitor.

3) KV-cache eviction edge case (canary logs)
- User case: intermittent decoding artifacts after context-switch (tokens repeated). Suspect KV-cache pointer/garbage when upgrading model version during in-flight sessions.
- Logs: `kv_cache_evicted_for_session=session-xyz, reason=mem_pressure, last_seq=1024` followed by repeated tokens reported by client.
- Quick notes:
  - add stronger invariants / sanity checks in session manager: when eviction happens, mark session as restarted or return definitive error to client instead of continuing opaque generation.
  - short-term: increase mem pool for canary to avoid eviction until invariant is implemented.
- TODO: add unit test that forces eviction mid-generation and asserts session terminated cleanly. (PR idea: `tests/session/eviction_handling_test.py`)

4) Kernel notes / tricks
- Important pins we've learned:
  - certain cuBLAS versions + triton 2.17 spike mem usage on attention backward/forward split kernels. Pin to cuBLAS 12.x for now.
  - quantized kernels (int8) give great perf but are more fragile with large seqs and KV-layout change. Add extra guard rails for quantized kernels on >2048 seqs.
- Commands I used today:
  - reproducer run: `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 ./bin/serve --model-path /mnt/models/llama-13b --profile`
  - capture perf: `sudo perf record -F 99 -p <pid> -g -- sleep 30 && sudo perf script > out.perf`
  - nvprof/traces: `nsys profile -o triton_trace --trace=cuda,osrt ./bin/serve ...`
  - flamegraph: `perf script | ./stackcollapse-perf.pl | ./flamegraph.pl > flame.svg`

5) Quick TODOs (personal)
- [ ] finish triage bisect for triton (today)
- [ ] open PR for seq_length_cap fallback routing (WIP)
- [ ] run synthetic load tests for batching heuristics (me)
- [ ] add eviction unit test and integration test (pair with Priya)
- [ ] doc short-term rollback plan for triton (for ops runbook)

6) Notes to self / meeting points
- Standup at 10:00 - call out canary artifacts and perf drop; propose short freeze on scheduler heuristic change until we validate.
- Postmortem: if triton is root cause, include timeline of infra bumps + commit hashes + mitigations (ops rollback, pinned versions).
- Remember to update confluence page: `confluence.redwood/srv/serving-runtime-incident-2026-03-06` after initial mitigation.

7) Misc fragments / ideas
- Explore heuristic: batch by KV-cache locality (prefer grouping requests hitting same KV memory pages) -> could increase cache hits and reduce memory churn. Needs prototype.
- Measure tail-latency impact of increasing small-batch priority (p99 improvement vs throughput loss).

End of scratchpad.

Links to related items (for follow-ups):
- GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/issues/423 (OOM long seq)
- JIRA: JIRA-RT-1129 (batching perf regression)
- Confluence: confluence.redwood/srv/KV-cache-design (design notes)
